text:
Priya (pm): drafting a short PRD for an adaptive fallback policy that balances latency, cost, and quality. Need quick input on acceptance criteria and edge cases from infra/runtime/security.
Jun (eng-platform): thanks — can you list the customer-driven constraints? e.g., no cross-region fallback unless >Xms, data residency flags, model-compatibility rules.
Priya (pm): customer asks: 1) avoid cross-region for EU customers unless region is degraded for >30s, 2) prefer quantized variant of same model if accuracy drop <3%, 3) failover to small model only if user-configured or >95% queue.
Alex (runtime): important: KV-cache incompatibilities between variants. If we fallback to a model with different tokenizer or context-length, we need plan for prefix re-encoding or graceful truncation.
Maya (sre): also watch for cascading load. If fallback increases per-request CPU on a different pool, we could overload that pool. Need h-circuit breaker per-pool.
Sam (cust-succ): real customer example: AcmeMaps wants EU-only unless downtime >2min, plus audit trail of fallback events. They want human-readable reason codes in logs.
Li (security): data residency: any cross-region fallback must have explicit customer opt-in, and keys must not leave region. For Private deployments, fallback to hosted is blocked by default.
Casey (design): from UX: include a small signal to app (status header) when fallback happens and a user-facing quality tag (e.g., "reduced-resolution") so product teams can surface it.
Jun (eng-platform): sketch of policy JSON we'd support:
```
{
  "tiers": ["premium","standard","best-effort"],
  "fallback_rules": [
    {"from":"premium","to":"standard","conditions":{"latency_ms":500}},
    {"from":"standard","to":"best-effort","conditions":{"queue_pct":95}}
  ],
  "region_constraints": {"cross_region_allowed": false, "override_after_s": 120}
}
```
Jun (eng-platform): note: we need to attach compatibility labels to models (tokenizer_id, max_ctx, quant_flags) and runtime check that tokenizers match.
Alex (runtime): acceptance criteria proposal: 1) policy enforces no cross-region fallback unless override_after_s elapsed and customer opt-in; 2) system prefers same-tokenizer variants and logs mismatch events; 3) automatic prefix re-encode only for compatible tokenizers; 4) fallbacks emit structured event with reason_code and metrics.
Maya (sre): operational gates: canary rollout to 5% of traffic, real-time circuit metrics in console, and auto-rollback if error-rate delta >1.5x baseline.
Li (security): add acceptance: keys never egress region for EU customers; fallback to hosted returns 403 unless explicit allowlist.
Priya (pm): edge cases to capture in PRD: expired KV cache when switching variants, partially streamed responses when fallback occurs mid-stream, simultaneous multi-tenant failover storms, and billing delta reporting.
Casey (design): UX edge cases: how to show mid-stream downgrade? propose showing a short system notice in client SDK and continue stream with ``[degraded]`` prefix.
Sam (cust-succ): can we expose a per-request header `x-fallback-reason`? customers asked for that.
Jun (eng-platform): yes, emits `x-redwood-fallback: region_override|quant_swap|tier_fallback` and also event to telemetry.
Priya (pm): next steps: I will draft PRD with the acceptance criteria above and a short runbook section. Can folks review the doc by EOD Friday?
Alex (runtime): I'll add compatibility-checker spec (tokenizer, ctx, quant).
Maya (sre): I'll write the canary / rollback playbook.
Li (security): I'll add the region/key gating language.
Casey (design): I'll mock the SDK header UX.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy queued for `adaptive-fallback-v0.1` -> scheduled 2024-05-14T16:00Z :rocket:
Priya (pm): thanks all :white_check_mark: I'll drop the PRD link here once ready.
